message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"16.21","verdict":"revise","checks":{"complete_coverage":true,"no_added_claims":true,"names_and_negations":true,"lexical_fidelity":true,"uncertainties_disclosed":false},"findings":[{"source_quote":"αὔ[ριον ἀπὸ] τῶν τοῦ διδασκάλου σου λόγων δείξω τὸν δημιουργὸν μὴ ἀνώτατον λέγοντα εἶναι θεόν.","english_quote":"tomorrow I will show from your teacher's words that he says the creator is not the highest God.","issue":"The teacher-speaker interpretation is contextually defensible, but the note does not preserve the materially different attachment available in the printed Greek: λέγοντα can agree directly with τὸν δημιουργόν, making the creator the speaker. The chosen interpretation instead supplies the teacher as the unexpressed object of δείξω and subject of λέγοντα, while taking τὸν δημιουργόν as the subject of εἶναι. The reference to the teacher's words supports that inference but does not make it explicit or uncontested.","suggested_revision":"Expand the lexical note to explain the chosen syntax and preserve the alternative: 'I will show from your teacher's words the creator saying that he is not the highest God.' State that the main rendering infers the teacher as speaker from τῶν τοῦ διδασκάλου σου λόγων, whereas the alternative attaches λέγοντα directly to τὸν δημιουργόν. The revised note and any revised English require fresh review; this ambiguity alone does not require a publication block.","severity":"major"},{"source_quote":"Τίς δὲ ἀνάγκη ἐὰν αὐτὸν ἐνταῦθα εἰσιόντα τὰς κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ βλασφημίας λέγειν;","english_quote":"What necessity is there to let him come in here and speak his blasphemies against God?","issue":"The translation defensibly understands ἐὰν as the infinitive 'allow,' normally accented ἐᾶν. The supplied print instead has the accent normally associated with the conditional conjunction ἐὰν. The accusative αὐτόν and infinitive λέγειν strongly support the permissive interpretation, but this accentual feature and interpretive decision are not disclosed. The verified printed reading must not silently be presented as though it were ἐᾶν.","suggested_revision":"Add a source_issues note quoting 'ἐὰν', retaining it as the supplied reading, and explaining that the English follows the contextually supported infinitive sense 'allow.' If giving 'ἐᾶν', label it explicitly as a proposed accentual normalization, not the printed reading. Do not diagnose an OCR error or require renewed print verification merely because of this confirmed accentuation.","severity":"minor"}]}]}
